report.tagline: Normal-looking Ray-Ban and Oakley glasses with a camera, speakers and Meta AI built in, made with EssilorLuxottica, and the surprise hardware hit of 2025.
report.simpleSummary: Ray-Ban Meta glasses look like ordinary sunglasses or spectacles, but they have a small camera, open-ear speakers and microphones. You can take photos and videos hands-free, listen to music, take calls, and say 'Hey Meta' to ask the AI what you are looking at or to translate a sign. They cost from about $299, close to normal designer glasses. In 2025 more than 7 million were sold, three times the year before, which made them the first smart glasses that many ordinary people actually wanted.

overview.whatItDoes: The glasses combine a 12 MP camera, open-ear speakers, five microphones and a Qualcomm chip in frames from Ray-Ban and Oakley. They connect to the Meta AI app on your phone. Users capture photos and video, livestream to Instagram or Facebook, listen to audio, take calls and use Meta AI by voice, including live translation and 'look and tell me' questions. Meta Ray-Ban Display (2025) adds a small screen in one lens and a Neural Band wristband that reads finger movements.
howItWorks: A buyer picks a frame style, lens type (sun, clear, transition or prescription) and buys online or in eyewear stores.
The glasses pair with the Meta AI app, which stores media and settings.
A button or 'Hey Meta' takes a photo or video; an LED light shows people nearby that it is recording.
Meta AI uses the camera and microphones to answer questions about what you see and hear.
A charging case gives several extra charges; the glasses last a few hours of active use.
EssilorLuxottica designs, makes and sells the frames; Meta builds the technology and software.
overview.valueProposition: Capture moments and get AI help without taking out your phone, in glasses you would wear anyway.

businessModel.summary: EssilorLuxottica makes and sells the glasses and books most of the hardware revenue; Meta supplies the technology and AI. Meta's real goal is strategic: owning the next device after the phone and putting Meta AI in front of users, even while Reality Labs loses billions.

revenueStreams.detail: Glasses sold through Ray-Ban, Oakley, opticians and electronics stores; revenue shared between EssilorLuxottica and Meta under their partnership.
Extra margin for EssilorLuxottica's lens business.
More time with Meta AI, Instagram and WhatsApp; no direct subscription today.

businessModel.pricing: Ray-Ban Meta from about $299 (Gen 1) and $379 (Gen 2); Oakley Meta HSTN about $399; Oakley Meta Vanguard about $499; Meta Ray-Ban Display about $799 with Neural Band. Prices as widely reported; prescription extra.
costDrivers: AI computing in Meta data centres for every query
R&D in Reality Labs, including AR display research
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $379 pair, the retailer and EssilorLuxottica take a large share and the parts cost perhaps $100 or more. Meta likely earns little or nothing per pair after its share and AI computing costs. The bet is long-term: if glasses replace some phone time, Meta owns a platform instead of renting space on Apple and Google phones. Reality Labs lost about $4.6 billion in Q2 2026 alone, so the glasses are part of a very expensive strategy.

growth.moat: Meta has a lead of several years, the exclusive partnership with EssilorLuxottica (which owns Ray-Ban, Oakley and huge optical retail) and its own AI. A rival needs both fashion brands and AI. Google is partnering with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, and Apple is expected to launch glasses, so the lead may shrink.

pmLessons: Start with what people already do. Glasses and sunglasses are worn daily, so adding smarts to a familiar form factor beat building a new gadget.
Design and brand matter as much as technology for wearables. Google Glass failed partly on looks.
Find the simple use case first (camera and audio), then add the big vision (AI and displays).
Partnerships can unlock distribution you cannot build yourself.
